name: Halftone Reveal
description: WebGL image rendered as a halftone print that the cursor wipes away to reveal the sharp photo underneath, with a fading trail, click bursts and an intro dot-growth animation.
contents: Single container with a full-size WebGL2 canvas showing one image as halftone
Cursor trail mask that reveals the original image through the dots
behavior: Image appears as a halftone print in mono, duotone or CMYK-style color, with dots growing in on load
Pointer movement paints a soft trail that reveals the sharp photo and fades after a delay
Click or tap creates an expanding reveal burst, up to 4 at once
Optional wander mode moves an automatic reveal point when the pointer is outside
Rendering pauses when offscreen, hidden, or idle
editableByProps: Halftone mode, dot shape, cell size, angle and dot scale
Ink, accent and paper colors, contrast, brightness, invert, roughness and misregistration
Reveal radius, softness, trail linger time, reverse reveal
Wander, click burst and intro toggles

needsCodeEdit.change: Change the maximum number of simultaneous click bursts

needsCodeEdit.where: SHAPES constant and the metric and reach functions in the VIEW shader

needsCodeEdit.change: Change the wander path of the automatic reveal

fixed: Root is h-full w-full, so the parent must have a defined height or the component collapses
No frame is included, it fills whatever container it is placed in
Requires WebGL2, renders nothing if unavailable
Source image must allow CORS (crossOrigin anonymous) to load as a texture
Values are clamped internally: cellSize 2-80, dotScale 0.2-2, roughness, misregistration and softness 0-1
Wander is disabled when the user prefers reduced motion
Reveal depends on pointer events, so touch devices only reveal while touching or on tap bursts
Changing src recreates the whole WebGL setup
The canvas is hidden from assistive tech and the image has no alt text

options.look: Single-ink halftone dots on paper color
options.useWhen: A classic newspaper or print look in one color

options.look: Two overlapping dot layers in ink and accent colors
Full-color halftone, CMYK on light paper or RGB on dark paper
options.useWhen: The photo should keep its colors in a print or screen-dot style
